articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.summary: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons
articles.keyPoints:
• U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons
• The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.
• Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Will bank manager accept Kayalvizhi Alagiri’s apology, asks Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan grants a day’s time for the police to find out if the victim, subjected to physical assault, would agree for closure of criminal prosecution against the accused

The Madras High Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) wanted to know whether a bank manager would be willing to accept an apology from former Union Minister M.K. Alagiri’s daughter Kayalvizhi Alagiri and agree for closure of a criminal case registered against her for allegedly slapping him supposedly due to anger management issues on July 20, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan directed the Inspector of Shastri Nagar police station in Adyar, Chennai to make sure that Harsheen Singh, a branch manager with State Bank of India, appears before the court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) to explain if he is willing to accept the apology and give a quietus to the issue than continuing the prosecution.

The direction was issued during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by Ms. Alagiri seeking a direction to the police to register a First Information Report (FIR) against the bank manager on the basis of a counter complaint lodged by her on July 25, 2026 accusing him of having subjected her to verbal abuse, aggressive intimidation and public humiliation.

Government Advocate (criminal side) S. Yogaraja Sekar told the judge that Ms. Alagiri was the owner of a commercial building in which the bank branch was functioning. There was a dispute between the landlady and the tenant over the non-functioning of an elevator in the building and a quarrel over that issue had led to a physical assault against the bank manager on July 20, 2026.

The police had intially registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Ms. Alagiri under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abusing and assaulting the bank manager. It also completed the investigation and filed a charge sheet before a Metropolitan Magistrate in Chennai. The Magistrate was slated to take up the case for hearing next on December 22, 2026, the law officer said.

In so far as the counter complaint lodged by the landlady against the bank manager was concerned, the Government Advocate said, the police had conducted a preliminary inquiry but did not find any material to substantiate any of the allegations levelled by her. Therefore, the investigating officer had dropped further action and closed her complaint, he added.
On his part, the petitioner’s counsel S.L. Sudarsanam said, his client would apologise, if necessary and in order to give a quietus to the entire issue.

articles.title: CJP’s Saurav Das claims he was stopped at Delhi airport from travelling to U.K.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In posts on X, Mr. Das said he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his 1 a.m. flight to London

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Monday (November 23, 2026) alleged that he was stopped from travelling to the U.K. to attend an event at the University of Oxford, where he was invited to speak on the "cockroach movement".
In posts on X, Mr. Das said he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his 1 a.m. flight to London.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that someone in power was jealous of Mr. Das receiving an invitation from the University of Oxford.
Mr. Das said, "I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford."

"This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement.
"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!" he said.
Mr. Das said he has been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union for a panel discussion.
"And that's why I was going to London. But as soon as I went to the immigration check, I came to know that my passport has been flagged," he said.
"Why is the government so scared of an educated youth going among educated people and having an intellectual discussion?
"I wish I was Nirav Modi. I wish I was Vijay Mallya. I wish I had looted thousands of crores from the banks..." he said.

articles.title: The Bilkis Bano order — justice deferred again
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The right to liberty cannot undermine a survivor’s dignity, voice and difficult quest for justice

“Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought,” said John Rawls in A Theory of Justice. The American political philosopher’s line is easy to admire yet hard to practice. When an institution cannot be trusted to hear a wronged person, the old maxim justice delayed is justice denied begins to sound less like a warning than a description.

For nearly a quarter of a century, Bilkis Bano, a survivor of the 2002 Gujarat riots who was gang-raped by 11 men while pregnant and lost some members of her family, has had to prove over and over again what happened to her was real, that it was a crime, and that the law should answer it. Each time, she has done so with a defiant courage that has become a testament to the Republic’s conscience. She now may have to do it again. On October 28, 2026, a Supreme Court Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale suspended the life sentences of two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering some members of her family, granting them bail pending their appeals. Ms. Bano told the media that she learnt of the order just a few days ago through the press. The counsel for the two men later issued a statement on November 21, rejecting Ms. Bano’s allegation that she was kept in the dark about the proceedings but asserting that she was not party even in High Court.

“It is still baffling to me that for the second time after this order was passed, I have not been summoned to appear before the Supreme Court, nor has anything been heard from me,” Ms. Bano said in a statement through her attorneys. It is a sentence that no citizen, for whatever reason he may have for taking the oath regardless of his opinion of the merits of the order, should find easy to read.

Every word counts here. This case is designed to elicit both outrage and defensive responses. No one is found “not guilty” in the order. The principles, which were upheld by the Bombay High Court in 2017, remain the same. What the Bench has done is that it has merely suspended the sentences of the two men, Bipinchand Kanhaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, until their appeals are disposed of, by pointing out that both men have been in jail for over 17 years, one of them has a severe disability, and their appeals raise questions of fact and law that require examination. The Additional Solicitor General opposed the pleas. The convicts’ appeals against the High Court’s judgment are still to be decided.

There is no objection to the order in the context of not subscribing to retributive or deterrent theories of punishment. However, at a time when there is talk of making the criminal justice system victim-centric, why was victimology forgotten in this case? That is the central question which survives despite the November 23, 2026 order by the same Bench releasing Siraj Pada, one of the convicts of the Sabarmati Express coach fire on similar grounds.

articles.title: Power outage during Minister’s programme in Kannur: KSEB staff rally behind suspended sub-engineer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Employees of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), under the banner of a joint action committee of officers and workers’ organisations, launched an agitation in Kannur on Monday (November 23) demanding the withdrawal of the suspension of sub-engineer Satheesh Babu in connection with a brief power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph on Saturday (November 21).

Hundreds of employees and officers from various KSEB offices joined the protest, with the organisations warning that the agitation would continue until the suspension was revoked. They also indicated that the protest could be extended across the State if the management failed to reconsider its decision.

The employees said the power supply had been disrupted for only about nine minutes as part of urgent maintenance work after a potentially dangerous fault was detected in an 11 kV feeder supplying the Kannur town area. They maintained that the interruption was necessary to avert a possible accident and that the required information had been communicated to consumers in advance through the outage management system and WhatsApp groups.

They alleged that neither the division office nor the section office had been informed about the Minister’s programme and that there was no question of deliberately disrupting the power supply. They also said that Mr. Babu had submitted an explanation when the authorities sought his response, but he was suspended without a proper preliminary inquiry.

The controversy erupted after the power disruption during the Electricity Minister’s programme at Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21. MLA T.O. Mohanan, who was present at the event, lodged a complaint with the KSEB chairman alleging deliberate disruption of the power supply. The suspension followed the complaint.

Inaugurating the protest in front of the KSEB office in Kannur, MLA K.V. Sumesh described the suspension as arbitrary, undemocratic and an insult to the dignity of the employees. He demanded its immediate withdrawal and warned that failure to do so would lead to a strong public agitation across the State.
He questioned the rationale behind suspecting an employee of deliberately disrupting power supply for political reasons, irrespective of which political front was in power.
“Employees could not be expected to compromise safety procedures because a Minister or an elected representative was attending a programme,” he said.

articles.title: Violence erupts in Pithapuram amid JSP councillors’ sparring over vice-chairman pick
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jana Sena Party Councillors, supporters opposed the party’s decision to elect Bojja Venkateswara Rao as Pithapuram Municipal Vice-Chairman on the grounds of being a newcomer to the party.

Rift within the Jana Sena Party boiled over into open violence in Pithapuram on Monday as a bitter power struggle over the Municipal vice-chairman post culminated in the alleged assault of Veeramareddy Chakri, the personal assistant of JSP’s Kakinada MP Tangella Uday Srinivas, by party supporters.

articles.title: Krushi OWS holds road safety awareness competitions for school students
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 250 students from various schools, including government schools in remote areas such as Paderu, participated in road safety awareness competitions organised by the Krushi Orthopaedic Welfare Society (Krushi OWS) at Alluri Seetharama Raju Vignana Kendram in the city on Sunday.

The programme featured painting, elocution, quiz, and short-film competitions to sensitise young people to road safety and the consequences of traffic accidents. Students from urban areas and distant places took part. Some of the short films highlighted the importance of wearing helmets and keeping tribal areas clean.

Dr. Kiran Kumar Nandivada, founder and CEO of Krushi OWS, orthopaedic spinal surgeon and rheumatologist, said the initiative aimed to create awareness about traffic violations and prevent accidents and disabilities. Founded in 1987, the society has been working for underprivileged people and persons with disabilities.

Recalling the severe injuries caused by road accidents, Dr. Kiran said such cases often required the involvement of several medical specialists and placed a considerable financial burden on families. He urged parents to discourage underage driving and guide children towards responsible road use.

The programme also showcased a video created using artificial intelligence by a visually impaired participant. Three Class VII students, two girls and a boy, who demonstrated knowledge of artificial intelligence, pledged to develop assistive devices for persons with disabilities.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.

The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Shenzhen offers an opening, but sustained engagement between Washington, Moscow and Beijing must now follow

For the first time since 1972, there is no treaty formally restricting the world’s largest nuclear arsenals. New START (New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty) expired in February, and nine months later, a successor treaty is still far from being drafted. Russia had offered to keep observing New START’s limits for a year if the United States did the same. Instead, the U.S. has pushed for an “improved” agreement, insisting that any nuclear treaty must involve China, which understandably has its own reservations.

On November 19, the leaders of the three countries met for the first time on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. They issued a joint declaration reaffirming that a nuclear war must never be fought. They also pledged subsequent talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. However, there are no provisions for the verification of compliance with these commitments, and no date seems to have been fixed for further talks. Despite Shenzhen, the underlying tension between the three countries’ positions remains. Each country’s position makes sense from where it sits, but at a time fraught with conflict, further complicated by emerging technologies, this treaty-less scenario cannot continue indefinitely.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.
Editorial Context: Core accountability: On core sector performance. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

📰 Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls

The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Pattabiram residents urge Highways dept. to build roundabouton CTH Road junction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Residents of Pattabiram have urged the Highways Department to build a roundabout on the Chennai–Tiruvallur High Road (CTH) or Chennai–Tirupati–Renigunta Road near the flyover, replacing the Level Crossing 2 on the railway siding.
Without a roundabout, the six-way junction presents a chaotic sight during peak hours, said Roy Rozario, a resident.
Apart from the lanes of the C.T.H Road, road to/from Poonamallee and M.G. Road join the junction. People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction.

“Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added.

Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist.
The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly.

“Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.
Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court in Mumbai on Saturday sent six minors to a juvenile correctional home till December 4 in connection with the alleged assault of a couple at a garden in Kurla on Friday evening, police said on Sunday. The six are aged between 12 and 15, the Ghatkopar police said.

articles.title: Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare services in the State.

Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant. He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department.
Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April. Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged.

Alleging that the “condition of the Radiology Department is also extremely concerning”, Mr. Batra said 10 of the 13 sanctioned faculty posts and nine of the 11 Senior Resident posts were vacant in the department, as per a September-October 2026 report. Of the nearly 500 patients advised ultrasound examinations daily, only 40% could undergo the test on the same day, he added.

Questioning the gap between budgetary allocations and the availability of health care facilities, Mr. Batra said ₹1,232 crore had been allocated to the Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences and PGIMS for 2026-27, an increase of ₹422 crore over the previous year, but patients continued to face shortages of medicines and delays in diagnostic tests.
Mr. Batra also raised concerns over two incidents of ceiling plaster falling in the old hospital building in October.

On behalf of the Congress, Mr. Batra demanded that all vacant posts be filled, medicine stocks and pending complaints be made public, diagnostic facilities expanded and old hospital buildings subjected to a safety audit.

“The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not speeches and announcements,” he said, adding that the Congress would continue to raise this serious issue concerning health and hold the government accountable.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement

The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22).

"The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail," the two parties said in a joint statement.
"A follow-up meeting will be held," they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.
But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.
His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".

fullParagraphs: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

articles.title: Wanted man held after 14 months for mob attack on Delhi police team in Chhatarpur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused, identified as Arbaj Khan alias Baiju, a resident of Chandan Holla village in Chhatarpur, was apprehended by the Special Staff of South district from Village Gadpur in Bhiwadi on November 20, police said

A 20-year-old man wanted in connection with a mob attack on police personnel in south Delhi’s Chhatarpur, in which four policemen were injured, has been arrested from Rajasthan after evading arrest for over 14 months, police said on Sunday (November 22, 2026)

The accused, identified as Arbaj Khan alias Baiju, a resident of Chandan Holla village in Chhatarpur, was apprehended by the Special Staff of South district from Village Gadpur in Bhiwadi on November 20, following a tip-off received two days earlier, police said.

According to the police, the incident took place on September 15, 2025, when a police team performing official duties in Chandan Holla village was attacked by a mob armed with bricks, sticks and stones. Four police personnel sustained injuries in the attack, while the mob also obstructed the team from carrying out its duties.
An FIR was registered at Fatehpur Beri police station on September 16, 2025, under sections 221, 132, 121(1), 110, 351(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Police said a team of the Special Staff developed the intelligence input about Khan’s whereabouts and conducted an operation in Bhiwadi to apprehend him. He was subsequently brought to Delhi and arrested on November 20 in connection with the case.
The police said the accused had no previous criminal involvement. Further investigation remains under way.

articles.title: Raut alleges BJP offers funds to secure support for Delimitation Bill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sanjay Raut alleged during the conference that an MP would receive ₹150 crore upon breaking away from a party to support the Delimitation Bill without facing disqualification

Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut alleged at a conference on November 22 that the Bharatiya Janata Party is offering ₹150 crore to Members of Parliament to gain backing for the Delimitation Bill, while also alleging that the government is delaying the session of the Parliament because it lacks the support of 40 to 45 MPs to pass the legislation and is attempting to pressure parties or buy lawmakers.
Editorial | Deservedly dead: On the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026

The Delimitation Bill contains a provision to increase the number of seats in the Lok Sabha to 850, which has resulted in a dispute between the National Democratic Alliance and the INDIA bloc, where the National Democratic Alliance states that carrying out delimitation is required by the Constitution to reflect data from a census and to enable reservation for women, while the Opposition demands implementation of 33% reservation for women within a Lok Sabha that contains 543 members.

Sanjay Raut alleged during the conference that an MP would receive ₹150 crore upon breaking away from a party to support the Delimitation Bill without facing disqualification, and he claimed that a Minister from Maharashtra has taken responsibility for the situation and promised to provide funds for the purpose, further alleging that the government has delayed the session of the Parliament because it does not concern itself with the nation, the Constitution, or the Parliament, adding that if parties do not defect, MPs would be purchased, and he referenced a statement regarding a rate on an exchange of ₹150 crore per MP.
Shiv Sena-Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray / Bharatiya Janata Party / National Democratic Alliance

articles.title: 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive spectator; experts call it contrary to spirit of constitutional checks and balance

With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years.
Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls

As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues.
They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary.

As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17 th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year.

“The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow.

Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”.

Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances.

“The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.
Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Mumbai Police to issue cards with QR code for identity checks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the measure on November 21, 2026, and cards were distributed to personnel, including traffic police, as part of steps to digitise the force

Mumbai Police will issue cards with QR code and NFC to personnel, and citizens can scan the code through the Mumbai Police Citizen App to check a person’s photograph, name, date of joining and posting, a measure that follows cases in which fraudsters posed as police and sought money from citizens.

Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the measure on Saturday (November 21, 2026), and cards were distributed to personnel, including traffic police, as part of steps to digitise the force. Mumbai Police states that printing has been completed, that personnel will receive cards within a month, that the project covers 51,308 posts and that the government sanctioned about ₹4 crore in February.

Personnel must carry the card while on duty, in uniform or not; officers who visit premises where people live, question citizens or approach people during investigations will have to carry it, so that those whom they approach can verify credentials; and a scan through the app directs users to a platform that displays photograph, name, date of joining and posting, which citizens can compare with the person who presents the card.

The card will have NFC technology, which personnel with authorisation can use for access to police establishments and for purposes, and the measure comes against a pattern in which criminals use cards that carry police identity and claim to be from crime branch to intimidate people into handing over cash or valuables, with fraudsters stopping citizens during walks and businessmen while claiming to conduct checks.

The system could offer a means of verification in scams in which fraudsters pose as police, CBI or officials from law enforcement during video calls and circulate cards with identity to establish credibility, and citizens can check credentials of anyone who claims to be a Mumbai Police officer rather than rely on a card.
Mr. Fadnavis said criminals use technology and police must stay ahead, and that technology works without bias and can improve efficiency.

articles.title: Central California concert shooting: Nine people shot; one in critical condition
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Authorities said that they believe the shooting ‘may be gang-related’ but didn’t elaborate
Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday (November 22).

The shooting broke out around 7:30 p.m. Saturday (November 21) at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare County, a mountainous region in the centre of the state, the county sheriff's department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced.

One 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and required surgery. He remained in critical condition, the sheriff's department said. Two other victims, ages 19 and 22, also required surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries.

Authorities said that they believe the shooting “may be gang-related” but didn't elaborate. The show in the town of roughly 3,000 people featured performers from neighbouring states, the department said.
The department didn't immediately respond to emailed questions seeking further details but said there was no longer any immediate threat to the public.

articles.title: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State BJP chief claims Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not language, as Bengali-speaking Hindus are now being persecuted and bearing the consequences of Partition
West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh .
“Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons.

Noting that India had played a crucial role in the creation of Bangladesh, the BJP Rajya Sabha MP expressed his opinion that Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not on the basis of the Bengali language.

“Bangladesh was not created for the sake of language. If it had been, Bengali-speaking Hindus in Bangladesh would not be dying like this today,” he said. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the fundamental question at that time should have been the protection of people and the creation of a democratic environment. Instead, the leadership surrendered to religious fundamentalism, he said.

Claiming that the wounds of Partition continued to haunt the subcontinent, the BJP leader said that it was religious minorities, particularly Hindus in Bangladesh, who were bearing the consequences. Blaming Partition on Jawaharlal Nehru and Mahatma Gandhi, Mr. Bhattacharya claimed that had Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose become independent India’s first Prime Minister, he would never have accepted the two-nation theory or allowed the subcontinent to be divided into India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

The remarks by the West Bengal BJP leader come at a time when fresh political tensions have erupted in Bangladesh. Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. Ms. Hasina has announced that she is keen to return to Bangladesh.

West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh .

“Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons.

Noting that India had played a crucial role in the creation of Bangladesh, the BJP Rajya Sabha MP expressed his opinion that Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not on the basis of the Bengali language.

“Bangladesh was not created for the sake of language. If it had been, Bengali-speaking Hindus in Bangladesh would not be dying like this today,” he said. articles.title: FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said
Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International, as it found its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe".
In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".
A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis.
"The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said.
Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added.

The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law. Hence, the FSSAI said it has granted sanction to launch prosecution under the FSS Act, 2006, against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd.

Through a social media post, FSSAI said it has sanctioned prosecution against a few other companies, including Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.
The regulator has suspended the licence of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance of rules and regulations.
FSSAI has also issued a product recall order against Asha Confectionery. The company has been asked to withdraw pre-pack chocolate filled cookies as they were found unsafe.
During this calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators (FBOs) and also e-commerce companies.

articles.title: SIR: Voters in Karnataka challenge deletions, say officials asking them to withdraw appeals, file Form 6
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who challenged their deletion, some of whom said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal

After the final electoral rolls from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were published, several people whose names had been deleted challenged their exclusion. They argued that they were left out despite having completed the entire process, including attending hearings and submitting the required documents.

More than 350 appeals have been filed across Karnataka so far. The Deputy Commissioner or District Election Officer (DEO) serves as the first appellate authority in the SIR, while the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) is the second and final appellate authority if the first-stage response is unsatisfactory. According to the CEO’s office, all appeals received so far remain pending or have been disposed of at the first appellate stage.

The Hindu spoke to several people in Bengaluru who have challenged their deletion. While some said officials advised them to withdraw their appeals and apply afresh through Form 6, others said officials had themselves submitted Form 6 applications on their behalf when they approached them seeking reversal of their deletion through an appeal. A few of them said they had since received an Elector’s Photo Identity Card (EPIC) and were told that their names would figure in a supplementary list.

While Form 6 applications are accepted throughout the year as part of the ECI’s “continuous updation” process, this route could leave those excluded from the SIR rolls unable to vote in the upcoming local body elections, including the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) elections. The GBA elections have been directed to be conducted using the SIR final rolls by December, before even the summary revision process begins or a supplementary list is published.

Those who have appealed argue that they are not new voters seeking fresh inclusion, but people who have been voting from the same addresses and were wrongly deleted. They also questioned why they should be asked to make a declaration through Form 6 that does not reflect their circumstances, when they had already submitted documents to address the discrepancies flagged during the SIR.

Iqbal, a resident of Sarjapura, told The Hindu that he received a notice over “no mapping.” He had mapped his father’s details, whose name is on the electoral roll in Bihar,but his name was still flagged. Mr. Iqbal said that although he had shifted his residence within the city more than five years ago, his EPIC had been updated and he had submitted the required documents. His name was deleted from the final SIR rolls after figuring in the draft list.

Several people also said that while the names of all members of their families figured in the draft rolls, some were deleted from the final list. They argued that even when appeals were disposed of, the outcomes were not uniform within families.

Sahiba, a resident of Jayanagar, said she was flagged over an anomaly indicating that the age gap between two children was less than nine months. She has twins and submitted their birth certificates to establish this. However, officials subsequently raised a discrepancy in her mother’s name across records. “I explained that it was the same person and that only the spelling had changed during translation. I submitted all my documents as well as my mother’s. But I was then questioned about why I had mapped to my mother and not my father or husband. Both my father and husband are in Saudi Arabia and were not part of the 2002 rolls. Now the officials are telling me to withdraw my appeal and file Form 6,” she said.

articles.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, says NYT
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment

Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia’s recent scandal , kept in contact with an official ​from China’s top spy agency for more than a year during ‌her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York ​Times reported on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Alice Huang was in ⁠touch with an officer from China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, ‌citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.
Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment. ⁠ Reuters has not been able to reach Alice ⁠Huang for comment.
Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia chip sales.
U.S. authorities have been investigating Megaspeed ​since 2024 over concerns it smuggled ‌Nvidia’s advanced AI chips to China.
Sunday’s (November 22, 2026) report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.
That October ‌29 article touched off a scandal that led ​to Jensen Huang’s resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia’s stock price.
Trump administration officials have ⁠repeatedly said they have not concluded that Alice Huang spied for China.
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said this month the Justice Department ‌had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.
U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton repeated that on Sunday.
