articles.title: Armenia drops Nagorno-Karabakh claim in proposed new constitution
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire

Armenian leader Nikol Pashinyan unveiled a draft constitution on Monday (November 23, 2026) that would get rid of a 1990 independence clause and claim to the disputed Karabakh region, saying it was the only way to reach a peace deal with Azerbaijan.
The Caucasus foes have been locked in a territorial conflict over the mountainous region since the fall of the Soviet Union.
In a 2023 offensive, Baku retook the Armenian-populated region, forcing a mass exodus, and has since demanded that Yerevan change its constitution for a peace treaty to be possible.
Mr. Pashinyan addressed Armenians, promising a peace treaty with Azerbaijan should his countrymen back the new constitution in a referendum.

Mr. Pashinyan said the new text rejects "the logic of the Declaration of Independence of August 23, 1990 — that is, the logic of conflict" and said the aim of the new constitution is to "ensure peace".

The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire.
Armenia's Opposition has accused Mr. Pashinyan of bowing to Azerbaijan's demands under pressure, calling it "Aliyev's Constitution" — after Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev.
But Mr. Pashinyan told Armenians not to believe "that we are doing this for someone else under external pressure".
Mr. Pashinyan — whose party is several seats short of a constitutional majority in Parliament — called on the Opposition not to block the referendum.
"If the people will vote against the constitution, I will resign," he said.

articles.title: India maps landslide susceptibility as part of shift from post-disaster relief to landslide management
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Mapping exercise covers 4.3 lakh square km; focus now on prevention, preparedness, risk reduction, says Science Minister; calls for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring to minimise impact

India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026).

He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy.

He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries.

Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.

The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.
Editorial Context: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

articles.title: Municipal staff transfers to move online by Tamil Nadu govt., with vacancies displayed on portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be eligible for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

The Tamil Nadu government has introduced online counselling for transfers and postings of employees in municipal corporations, municipal councils and town panchayats, covering employees in the lower and middle levels of the government pay structure, including posts such as assistants, junior assistants and superintendents. The guidelines were issued through two Government Orders (G.O.s) by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department dated November 19, 2026.
The counselling will be based on vacancies and station seniority. The online portal is being developed by the respective heads of departments and will be introduced shortly, an official said.

Regarding whether employees would be able to raise grievances relating to seniority or other issues through the portal, the official said the department would be asked to incorporate a provision for submitting representations online. The portal would also provide details of vacancies and the procedure for applying for transfers, he said.

According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be liable for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

Transfers during the non-transfer period, between June 1 and March 31, will be permitted only on administrative grounds, including promotions, disciplinary reasons, complaints, long leave arrangements and other administrative exigencies.

All transfers, including those sought by employees, during the transfer period will be processed through the online portal. The guidelines also provide for a maximum of three alternative station preferences in transfer applications.
The official said counselling for Executive Officers of town panchayats had already been conducted and postings issued based on it.

articles.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.
Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.
After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.
Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress.

“Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. Haldane and Laurie Baker. Gandhi, he said, derived his principles from all traditions and belief systems – Jainism, Vaishnavism, Christianity, and even communism. His attitude to gender, religion, or non-violence evolved through his engagements with various philosophies.

“I do not see him as a quintessentially Hindu thinker, quintessentially Indian thinker, [or] quintessentially traditional thinker. He transcends these lanes. Or Leftist, Rightist, Conservative; he is all three,” Dr. Guha added.

On the question of caste and the equations with the Ambedkarite principles, Dr. Guha said that Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper caste while Ambedkar was a dalit without emancipation and they could only take those paths. From the perspective of history and the future of India, the paths are converging. Asked if Gandhi’s methods are lost in the era of social media, he said the “cockroaches showed that they have it”. If the book came out a few months later, he said he would have added a few paragraphs on the Cockroach Janata Party movement.

articles.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives.

The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors.

“No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore.

“We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu.

The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added.

While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. Santhosh, president of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Consumers Association.

In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges. These are not applicable because the court has stayed the green energy open access policy of the State, he added. More sub-stations and solutions for right of way challenges to lay lines on lands belonging to various government departments are among the other issues faced by investors that threaten to slow down solar energy projects.

articles.title: Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs inaugurated in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress Member of Parliament Shashi Tharoor on Saturday inaugurated the Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs at the C. P. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation (CPRAF) to mark the institution’s 60th anniversary.

He also released two books, Heritage, Education and Nature – 60 years of the C.P.Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation, and A catalogue of Ravi Varma’s Oleographs and Chomo Lithographs. Speaking during the launch, Mr. Tharoor, a long-time friend of the family, said as an MP for Thiruvananthapuram, he represented a city and a region whose history is closely connected with both Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer and Raja Ravi Varma. To find their legacies brought together here in Chennai in an institution that has spent 60 years serving the wider public, is a particularly happy conjunction of history.
He said the lithographs of Raja Ravi Varma, while becoming familiar objects across the country, also allowed the many who were barred from entering temples to worship the deities as well.

One of the most significant reforms associated with Sir C.P.’s term as Dewan of Travancore was the temple entry proclamation, he added. He praised the work of the various schools run by the Foundation. including the Saraswathi Kendra in Chennai that was the city’s first school for children with autism, dyslexia and learning disabilities.

Former Madras High Court judge P. N. Prakash, who received the first copies of the books, said that Sir C.P. had a magnetic personality, was a tennis player, and a polyglot who could speak several languages including, French and Latin; and he was the youngest Advocate General of Madras High court.

Chairman and managing director of Seshasayee Paper & Boards Ltd., N. Gopalaratnam, said that Sir C.P. was very close to the Sesashayee Brothers and had helped them to put up FACT, PCC and many other industries. He was instrumental in starting hydroelectric projects including Pykara, Lower Bhavani Scheme and the one at Mettur Dam. “As a schoolboy, I have had the opportunity to watch him speak on two occasions. Though I did not understand everything that he spoke, his image as a majestic, well-dressed man lingers in my mind.”

Elaborating on the work done by the Foundation over the past 60 years, its president Nanditha Krishna said that the C.P. Art Gallery was established as the city’s first craft gallery to creeate a bridge between ancient craftsmanship and contemporary society. The Foundation introduced puppetry as a teaching aid, and trained and encouraged women. It established The Grove School, Rangammal Vidyalaya in Kancheepuram and the Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar Memorial School in Kumbakonam. Its Each One Teach One Initiative, launched by Shakuntala Jagannathan, in 1997, provides scholarships to children.
Prashanth Krishna, director of CPRAF and senior advocate and grandson of Sir C.P., Aryama Sundaram spoke.

articles.title: FUJIFILM’s Spectrum tour enthrals visual creators, photography enthusiasts in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The three-day event featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture
A multi-city FUJIFILM India Spectrum Tour, bringing together of the brand’s entire range of imaging solutions from Instax cameras, digital cameras and lenses, concluded in Bengaluru recently.

The three-day event, held at the Venkatappa Art Gallery, featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture, attracted a large number of people.

Company executives highlighted the regional strategy behind selecting the city for this segment of the tour. "We are excited to connect with the city’s vibrant imaging community. Through Spectrum, we aim to bring our imaging heritage and cutting-edge technology closer to creators,"’ said Koji Wada, managing director of FUJIFILM India.

The tour was in Bengaluru after Gurugram and Ahmedabad, attracting local photography enthusiasts, visual creators and students who prefer to have a hands-on experience with FUJIFILM product ranges. A central component involved educational masterclasses led by established industry practitioners. Photographers including Sudhir Ramachandran and Prashant Godbole were among the participants.

Sessions covered architectural, landscape, and street photography. Other sessions led by technical experts covered niche genres such as astrophotography, wildlife documentation, and sports imaging. The event consolidated the company’s various product categories, including mirrorless camera systems, instant photography devices, and optical tools, under a unified interactive environment.

Arun Babu, associate director of the Imaging Solutions Division at FUJIFILM India, said, “In Bengaluru, through hands-on experiences, we encouraged visitors to experiment with our imaging solutions and discover new ways to express their creativity.”

Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

“For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. articles.title: TDP defends venue choice for Vijayawada Mayor swearing-in, slams YSRCP for making it an issue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vijayawada MP says there is no rule stating that the event has to be held at the VMC council hall; YSRCP corporators submit a representation to NTR District Collector seeking his intervention

TDP leader and MP Kesineni Sivanath (Chinni) on Saturday (November 21, 2026), said that the decision to conduct the oath-taking ceremony for the Vijayawada Mayor and corporators on November 23 at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Kala Vedika was taken as a mark of respect to honour the ideals of the leader. The remarks come in the wake of YSRCP leaders raising a hue and cry about the choice of the venue for the event.

Addressing the media at NTR Bhavan in the city, the MP said they are not flouting any rules by choosing a venue other than the council hall of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC). “We sought permission from the State Election Commission for the event, and we have received it,” the MP said, referring to a rule that the ceremony can be held either at the council hall or at any convenient place within the VMC jurisdiction.
“There is no rule stating that the event has to be held at the council hall,” Mr. Sivanath said, hitting back at the YSRCP for making an issue out of it.
Mayor Vangaveeti Radha Krishna said Jai Bhim is not merely a phrase for the NDA, but a motto that reflects their decisions and actions.
The MP said the NDA created history by sweeping the VMC elections, and now it was time for them to focus on issues plaguing the city.
NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha receiving a representation from YSRCP corporators over the venue for the Mayor’s swearing-in ceremony, in Vijayawada on Saturday. | Photo Credit: G.N. RAO
Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) corporators submitted a representation to NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha, urging him to take steps to ensure the event is held at the VMC council hall.

The corporators said that the ceremonies had traditionally been held in the council hall since the establishment of Vijayawada Municipal Corporation, and expressed reservations over the arrangements for the event being made outside the hall.

They emphasised that the council hall held historical significance and represented institutional importance of the municipal corporation. They urged the Collector to respect the existing tradition and take necessary steps to hold the swearing-in ceremony at the hall.

As per a statement issued by them, Mr. Lakshmisha assured the corporators that necessary steps would be taken to ensure the smooth conduct of the swearing-in ceremony without causing inconvenience to anyone.

fullParagraphs: ‘Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead,’ said S. Jaishankar

India and Bulgaria on Saturday (November 22, 2026) reviewed their bilateral cooperation in trade, security, technology and other areas, even as the two sides also held discussions on IMEC, the Black Sea situation and the Ukraine conflict.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with his Bulgarian counterpart, Velislava Petrova, at the Hyderabad House in Delhi.

"Pleased to meet FM Bulgaria @vpetrova_mfa this afternoon. Reviewed our bilateral cooperation, including in trade, connectivity, investments, technology, security and talent mobility. Appreciated growing P2P linkages & cultural exchanges between our two countries, as well as deepening India-EU ties," Mr. Jaishankar later posted on X.

Agreed that the India-EU FTA should be followed through by "vigorous exchanges between our businesses". Also exchanged views on the prospects of IMEC (India Middle East Europe Economic Corridor) and other connectivity initiatives, he added.
"Appreciated the discussion on the Black Sea situation and the Ukraine conflict," the EAM said in his post.

In his opening remarks during their meeting, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead."

He said Ms. Petrova's visit was taking place when India is "also intensifying our relationship with the European Union, and we again thank you for all the support that you have extended to that process".

The entry into force of the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which India expects soon, will certainly provide a "new dynamism to that relationship, and when it comes to trade, technology, talent, we expect to do much more with Europe," the EAM said.

Mr. Jaishankar, during the meeting, also conveyed to her India's condolences to the "families who lost their loved ones in the tragic road accident" recently and wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

"I also want to take this opportunity to thank you for the support that your government has extended for the repatriation of our seafarers in the ships that were attacked in the Black Sea and looking after some of them who had sustained injuries," he added.

articles.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early
The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs.

A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her.

The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources.

Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early.

Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream.

“People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says.

A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics.
State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward.
“We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

articles.title: Clamour to reintroduce adequate number of air-conditioned buses in Kochi grows louder
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses.

While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns.

Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said.

With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added.

Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 22 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Clamour to reintroduce adequate number of air-conditioned buses in Kochi grows louder

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses.

While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns.

Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said.

With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added.

Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

⚡ 3-Point Exam Takeaway & Deep Breakdown
1. Core Context & Background: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

articles.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said
Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday (November 21, 2026), causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

"As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the Interior Ministry said on X, without specifying the location.
Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco.
Iran's Fars news agency reported the Revolutionary Guards had "attacked two U.S. bases, Sheikh Isa and Juffair, on the island of Bahrain in response to the illegal actions of the United States".

The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping line.
The U.S. military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

Iranian deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally."
"Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state TV.
Iran's demands include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

articles.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing
Thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on ​Saturday (November 21, 2026) despite heavy rain to protest against soaring living ‌costs, a deepening housing crisis and low wages.
Organiser ​CGTP, Portugal’s largest trade union federation, called ⁠for higher wages and pensions, lower prices for essential goods and services, and measures to curb housing costs.
The ‌CGTP said turnout reached “many thousands” as protesters carrying umbrellas and wearing hooded ponchos marched ‌along two of Lisbon’s main avenues. Police ‌did ⁠not provide an estimate.

“We work more, we ⁠have more expenses and we don’t have money for day-to-day life,” said Manuel Gomes, 44, a factory worker, arguing that the ​centre-right government’s policies ‌had made matters worse.

Protestors demanding affordable housing and carrying a banner with the words "Fight for our future, not in their wars" walks past a Christmas market in downtown Lisbon, on November 21, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP
“Our wages are low, diesel and gasoline prices keep going up, and so do housing costs and everything else. We have ‌to change this,” Gomes said.

Portugal’s average annual earnings ​in 2025 were 37% below the European Union average, according to Eurostat. Inflation ⁠hit 3.8% in October, driven by food and energy prices amid continuing tensions in the Middle East.

Portugal is ‌also grappling with one of Europe’s most severe housing affordability crises. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, hitting younger people particularly hard.

Luis Russo (66), a retired IT technician, said he ‌was demonstrating to demand “higher wages and pensions and against speculation in ​the rental market”, accusing the government of serving “big interests” rather than ordinary people.

The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing. Turnout at largely peaceful protests in France on Saturday was lower than ​in previous weeks.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

The story so far: The battle for the most-sought-after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer. On November 16, the U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule (IFR) requiring companies to have licences to supply advanced American AI chips to data centre operators outside the U.S. with substantial computing power to businesses headquartered in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. The new rule restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry”. The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but Congress strengthened the extant legal framework only during the first Trump term when it passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It strengthened the U.S. government’s authority to control the movement of advanced technology originating in the country, and included curbing exports of sensitive technologies, including top-tier chips, with dual-use — both commercial and military — applications to countries such as China, Russia, and Iran.

A year later, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Chinese telecom equipment maker Huawei and its affiliates on the Entity List, effectively blocking their access to high-end semiconductors.

articles.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow’ read a statement

Gadi Eisenkot , who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
Mr. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday (November 22), reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government".
Former military chief Mr. Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Mr. Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.

Saturday's (November 21) announcement comes as Mr. Eisenkot's wide-ranging anti-Netanyahu camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties and Arab-majority lists, or form a national unity government with Mr. Netanyahu's bloc.

"In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow [November 22]," the party said in a statement.
It added that it would "leave no stone unturned as it works to make bold moves possible and secure the breakthrough needed to form a government".

Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, an important figure in Mr. Eisenkot's camp, on Saturday (November 21) called for a "Zionist unity government headed by Eisenkot" and said his party would refuse to join up with Mr. Netanyahu or his bloc.

In a statement, Mr. Bennett said he was "committed to ensuring that Netanyahu will not be the next Prime Minister of the State of Israel, and my party will not join him or his bloc under any circumstances", he added.
Mr. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for a national unity government, which he says is needed to guarantee Israel's security.
Mr. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Mr. Netanyahu's Likud, but has previously ruled out serving in a government led by Mr. Netanyahu himself.

articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court ordered that six persons in the 12- to 15-year-old age group be placed in a juvenile home until December 4, after Ghatkopar police detained eight persons below 18 in connection with an assault on a couple at Pramod Mahajan Garden in Kurla on Friday evening (November 20, 2026) and produced all eight before the Juvenile Justice Board, police said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, an officer said.

According to police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of persons in the 12-15 age group surrounded them and began to abuse them; when the couple tried to reason with the group, the persons assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden, and police detained the eight after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.

Police said they were recording statements from the couple and the persons below 18 to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident, and an officer said, “We are finding out what was the reason for the assault.”

Samajwadi Party’s Maharashtra unit president Abu Asim Azmi said the age for juveniles should be brought down from 18 to 15 and said persons below 18 who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not receive concessions under the law; he said the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination.

Nitesh Rane, a BJP leader, commented on the video, saying, “This isn’t their father’s Pakistan,” and added that he “would send a person who wore a skullcap and had a beard to Aurangzeb if an incident happened again.”

BJP leader Kirit Somaiya, who was an MP, visited the garden on Saturday (November 21), met the couple at Ghatkopar police station, sought action, and said he would raise concerns about security with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.

NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the home portfolio, to adopt a policy of no tolerance when incidents occur and said citizens should be able to move around freely; Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui condemned the assault and said police were doing their job.

Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court ordered that six persons in the 12- to 15-year-old age group be placed in a juvenile home until December 4, after Ghatkopar police detained eight persons below 18 in connection with an assault on a couple at Pramod Mahajan Garden in Kurla on Friday evening (November 20, 2026) and produced all eight before the Juvenile Justice Board, police said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, an officer said.

According to police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of persons in the 12-15 age group surrounded them and began to abuse them; when the couple tried to reason with the group, the persons assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden, and police detained the eight after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.

Police said they were recording statements from the couple and the persons below 18 to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident, and an officer said, “We are finding out what was the reason for the assault.”

Samajwadi Party’s Maharashtra unit president Abu Asim Azmi said the age for juveniles should be brought down from 18 to 15 and said persons below 18 who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not receive concessions under the law; he said the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination.

Nitesh Rane, a BJP leader, commented on the video, saying, “This isn’t their father’s Pakistan,” and added that he “would send a person who wore a skullcap and had a beard to Aurangzeb if an incident happened again.”

BJP leader Kirit Somaiya, who was an MP, visited the garden on Saturday (November 21), met the couple at Ghatkopar police station, sought action, and said he would raise concerns about security with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.

NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the home portfolio, to adopt a policy of no tolerance when incidents occur and said citizens should be able to move around freely; Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui condemned the assault and said police were doing their job.

articles.title: i-ALERT system leads to savings, lesser emissions for RTC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month

The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) announced that they are the first State Road Transport Corporation in India to introduce the i-ALERT system in its BS-VI buses and indicated its implementation has saved the organisation approximately ₹36 crore in diesel costs.

According to the state-run road transport undertaking, the i-ALERT tool monitors and assesses driving patterns. It keeps tabs on gear selection, engine RPM, idling, overspeeding and braking practices, thus assisting drivers to adopt safer and more fuel-efficient driving methods.

The system was installed in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses has helped save 6,603 litres of high-speed diesel (HSD) a day and 1,98,090 litres a month. The corporation estimates its monthly savings at ₹2 crore.

The reduction in fuel consumption has also cut carbon emissions. With every litre of diesel estimated to generate 2.56 kg of carbon emissions, the initiative has helped reduce CO2 emissions by 16.90 metric tonnes a day, 507.11 tonnes a month and 6,169.84 tons annually, the TGSRTC stated.

The system also enables the corporation to assess individual driver performance after every duty and provide feedback and grades. Drivers are monitored for adherence to the prescribed Green Band RPM range, efficient use of economy gears, reduction in engine idling, avoidance of over speeding and appropriate braking practices.

TGSRTC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Anil Kumar congratulated the engineering department for adopting the technology. He urged other departments to adopt modern technology to further improve the corporation’s services.
APSRTC and KSRTC have approached senior TGSRTC officials seeking information on the performance of the i-ALERT system, the corporation said.

articles.title: U.P. Police mistakenly give guard of honour to Owaisi in Saharanpur, probe ordered
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police team had reached the circuit house in the morning to prepare for a Supreme Court judge's arrival; however, the judge had not reached the premises when Asaduddin Owaisi arrived there, and the personnel reportedly got confused

Police personnel in Saharanpur on Saturday (November 21, 2026) mistakenly gave a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi at the circuit house, apparently mistaking him for a Supreme Court judge who was scheduled to visit the premises, prompting an inquiry into the incident.

The police team had reached the circuit house in the morning to prepare for the judge's arrival. However, the judge had not reached the premises when Mr. Owaisi arrived, and the personnel reportedly got confused and accorded him the ceremonial salute.
Mr. Owaisi's visit to the circuit house was apparently not part of his original programme, and he arrived there unexpectedly, according to local inputs.

Mr. Owaisi was in the district, accompanied by Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) chief Chandrashekhar Aazad. The two leaders were in Saharanpur to hold a joint press conference ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
Mr. Owaisi stood and accepted the salute as the police personnel accorded him the guard of honour.
The two leaders had recently announced the formation of the Samajik Parivartan Morcha (SPM), a joint political front to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
In a statement, Saharanpur Police said the senior superintendent of police has directed the superintendent of police (Rural) to investigate the incident.
"Action as per rules will be ensured on the basis of facts and evidence obtained after the inquiry," the police said.
The incident has raised questions over the apparent lapse in identifying the person for whom the ceremonial honour was being arranged.
Guard of honour is a ceremonial military or police salute in which personnel stand in formation to honour designated dignitaries on official or formal occasions.

articles.title: The new BJP team’s piecemeal reset
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Apart from the usual distribution of organisational berths to poll-going States, caste groups, and other demographics of sex and age, the new BJP team reflects the party’s attempts at a reset. Nistula Hebbar reports on how three terms in power have brought both the pieties of the past and anxieties of the future into focus

Prime Minister Narendra Modi walked into a meeting of the newly appointed Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national office-bearers on August 22. The 64 office-bearers present assumed he would address them on how they should approach their assignments. Instead, he spent the next four-and-a-quarter hours individually querying them on their past organisational work.

The exchange was unhurried, with PM Modi at one point telling the audience that he too was once like them, a national office-bearer of the party during the late Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s tenure as Prime Minister (1999-2004), say some of the new office-bearers.

The identification was interpreted in some quarters as a pep talk to the new team of how far organisational service can take you in the BJP, but for others it pointed to a unifying characteristic in a list of names that otherwise lacked a meta narrative, and instead, in a piecemeal fashion exhibited the political anxieties of the BJP.

This privileging of organisational experience by the Prime Minister was the highlight of the new team. The BJP, now in its third term in power and seeking a fourth in 2029, is, with this new team, attempting a reset amid various political anxieties.

Journalist Shekhar Iyer, who has tracked the BJP for decades, says, “The new team marks a big shift in the party top brass’ approach to the challenges ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha poll. Increasingly, the BJP is signalling to itself that, henceforth, the chosen men and women will represent less of their individual personality and more of their abilities and capabilities for the tasks to be accomplished.”

articles.title: Indian-origin man detained in Texas after serving sentence for visual recording conviction
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Raghul Anandakrishnan's custody has been assumed from a Texas county jail, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a post on November 22

A 29-year-old Indian-origin man has been taken into custody by Federal immigration authorities in Texas following his conviction for attempted invasive visual recording, and he will remain detained while immigration court proceedings are pending, authorities said.
Raghul Anandakrishnan's custody has been assumed from a Texas county jail, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a post on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

In an official post on X , Raghul Anandakrishnan served time in a county jail in Texas after his conviction for attempted invasive visual recording. The conviction came after a woman reported that an employee at a wireless company went through her phone and transferred explicit photos of her from her phone to his.
"ICE took custody of him from the county jail. He'll remain in ICE custody pending immigration court proceedings," the post said.

The detention follows a June criminal case in Austin, where Austin Police Department records and Travis County court filings cited by local media showed Anandakrishnan was arrested while employed at a Total Wireless store.
According to court affidavits, he sent two intimate images from a customer's phone to his own device via AirDrop and accessed the customer's Snapchat account.

Travis County jail records show he was initially booked on June 7 on charges of invasive visual recording and computer security breach under a combined $10,000 bond and placed under no-contact orders before later being convicted of attempted invasive visual recording.
Federal officials have not immediately released details regarding his immigration status, current detention facility, or upcoming immigration court dates.

articles.title: South Korea Education Minister resigns amid AI cheating scandal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score
South Korea's Education Minister resigned on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted ahead of the country's key college entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial college entrance exam known as the Suneung.
The annual nine-hour Suneung is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country.

The confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures — including blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons but Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam.

"The exam concluded without any major incidents... However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance," Mr. Choi wrote on X.
"Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation," he added.
President Lee Jae Myung has accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday (November 16, 2026) whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied: "Due to my age, I am not confident I could."
Mr. Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday's (November 19, 2026) exam, where a vice minister instead announced the preventive measures.

Officials said 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during Thursday's (November 19, 2026) exam, nearly half of which were detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones that test takers had failed to hand over.

articles.title: North Korea delays international marathon until October: tour agency
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: It was held last year for the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, but this year's race, scheduled for April, was cancelled with no reason given

North Korea has postponed its annual international marathon, which gives runners from around the world a rare glimpse of the secretive state's capital city, by six months until next October, a tour agency has said.

The race, which has historically seen hundreds of local and foreign athletes pound the streets of Pyongyang before finishing in front of thousands of fans at Kim Il Sung Stadium, is the diplomatically isolated state's largest international sporting event.
It was held last year for the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, but this year's race, scheduled for April, was cancelled with no reason given.
The next edition, initially slated for April 2027, will now take place in October, Beijing-based Koryo Tours, which describes itself as the marathon's exclusive partner, said.

The company "has been informed by our partners in the Pyongyang International Marathon Committee that the date for the 2027 marathon is being changed", it said on its website on Saturday (November 22, 2026).
"It will not take place in April 2027. Instead, it is almost certain that the 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon will happen in October 2027," it added.
"We hope to have a fully confirmed date in good time," it said, without giving a reason for the change.
Last year's race, the first in six years, drew about 200 foreign runners who competed alongside more than 200 North Koreans. Local athletes won both the men's and women's events.
The number of foreign participants was significantly lower than 2019, when about 950 foreigners competed.
But the North cancelled this year's race, with Koryo Tours announcing in March that the decision had been confirmed by the country's athletics association.

articles.title: COP31: Turkiye's final draft doesn't mention the words ‘fossil fuels’ that cause global warming
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: COP31 President Murat Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary

The newest and possibly final proposed agreement to come out of United Nations climate talks doesn't contain the words fossil fuels , the chief cause of global warming, or specifically call for transitioning away from the coal, oil and gas that spew carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

The draft from Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum, president of the two-week conference in Antalya, Turkiye, called COP31, was released in the wee hours of Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning. Mr. Kurum gave negotiators only about three hours to make objections or ask for changes before the wording goes before the conference plenary.

There must be near-unanimous consensus for approval and several countries earlier in negotiations made vociferous objections to omitting a call to phase out fossil fuels. But the proposal does put a specific goal on a technology, supported by the oil industry, of capturing carbon pollution and storing it.

Because the text went to negotiators and the public after 3 a.m., countries and activists did not immediately respond to the newest version. The conference was scheduled to end Friday (November 20, 2026) and is now in double overtime . Organisers worry that as negotiators depart there may not be a voting quorum of 2/3 of the delegates, which would prevent passage of the draft.

Earlier in the week, Panama vowed to formally object to a final agreement that didn't put a cap on oil production, acknowledge failing goals to limit warming and beef up finance for nations to adapt to warming's harms. Panama Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro said the talks were being held hostage by a “petroleum mafia” and need to be reformed.

Fossil fuels also went unmentioned in final decisions for more than 25 years, mostly because of objections by Saudi Arabia, said Alden Meyer, a longtime analyst with the European think-tank E3G. He added, however, that the world agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” in Dubai in 2023.

“It would be a real setback if we come out of here with no signal that we were serious about what we agreed to do three years ago,” Mr. Meyer said.

The proposed final agreement makes a reference to the Dubai agreement in the first line, saying it is “recalling the United Arab Emirates Consensus in its entirety,” but the words “fossil,” “oil” or “coal” or “phase out” do not appear anywhere in the 10-page text.
